messages.content: Help me execute a callback function named 'processResult' that handles an error 'null' and a result value of 'Operation successful'?

function.name: invokeCallback
function.description: This function invokes a callback with an error and a value. If the callback throws an error, it is caught and re-thrown asynchronously. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

callback.description: The callback function to be invoked. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

error.description: The error to pass to the callback function. Can be 'null' if there is no error. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

value.description: The value to pass to the callback function. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

function.name: invokeCallback

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool functions.invokeCallback with JSON arguments. The callback is a string representation of a function? It says "This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation." So we provide the function as a string. For example: "function(err, val) { console.log('err', err); console.log('val', val); }". But the user wants to execute a callback function named 'processResult' that handles an error 'null' and a result value of 'Operation successful'. So maybe they want to define a function processResult(err, val) { ... } and then invoke it. But the tool expects a callback function string. We could provide "processResult" but that's not a function definition. The tool expects a function definition string. So we should provide something like "function processResult(error, value) { console.log('Error:', error); console.log('Value:', value); }". Then error: null, value: 'Operation successful'.

Thus we call the tool.
